findings.reason: arXiv 2608.16195 'RoboStriker: Latent-Space Strategic Games for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing' (submitted 2026-08) is textually and structurally very close to the already-listed arXiv 2601.22517 'RoboStriker: Hierarchical Decision-Making for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing' (submitted 2026-01, README.md line ~91), with an overlapping author team (Kangning Yin, Zhe Cao, Wentao Dong, Weishuai Zeng, Tianyi Zhang, Qiang Zhang, Jingbo Wang, Jiangmiao Pang, Ming Zhou, Weinan Zhang). Both use the same project name, near-identical phrasing ('hierarchical framework', 'distills ... into a structured latent manifold', 'Latent-Space Neural Fictitious Self-Play', 'available at RoboStriker'), and 2608.16195 reads like an expanded/rewritten resubmission of the same project (with an added theoretical Nash-game framing) rather than an independent new paper. Not added to the README pending a human decision on whether to treat it as an update to the existing 2601.22517 record, a second distinct entry, or a replacement.

findings.reason: arXiv 2608.01826 'Multi-View Unified Camera Fields: Geometry-Shaped Action-Facing Representations for RGB-Only Multi-Camera VLA Policies' is primarily a general multi-camera VLA representation-learning paper; its substantive quantitative results (98.9% LIBERO, +22.4 LIBERO-Plus, +23.3 pts across six RoboTwin tasks, all under a GR00T-N1.6 backbone) are on non-humanoid simulated tabletop/dual-arm benchmarks. The abstract's only humanoid-related claim is one trailing, detail-free sentence ('Real-world humanoid experiments further provide evidence of its practical effectiveness under RGB-only deployment') with no platform name, task description, or metric. Not added to the README because the humanoid contribution could not be substantiated as primary from the abstract alone; a human should check the full paper before deciding whether it belongs in the list.

findings.reason: arXiv 2608.09762 'Efficient Real-World Online Reinforcement Learning for Robot Manipulation via Centralized Training and Critic Decomposition' evaluates its centralized-training/critic-decomposition RL method mainly on two physical (non-humanoid) robotic arms doing pick-and-place and pot-reset tasks under large domain randomization; a simulated humanoid appears only as one additional validation environment, not the primary platform. Not added to the README because the humanoid contribution is a minor secondary result on a tabletop-arm-primary paper; a human should check the full paper to confirm how substantive the humanoid results are before deciding whether it belongs.

findings.reason: The 2026-08-19 PM run re-swept the window flagged incomplete by the AM run (2026-07-01..2026-08-19) using arXiv's advanced search (cs.RO, query "humanoid", sorted by announced date) and paginated fully through four pages without hitting rate limiting, down past 2607.00642 into 2606.xxxxx ids (confirming no July/August entries were skipped this time). Of 66 arXiv ids not yet in data/papers.json, 2 were left untouched because they are already tracked above (2608.16195 possible-duplicate-followon, 2608.01826 borderline-scope), 25 were excluded on unambiguous out-of-scope titles alone (pure social-HRI/psychology studies, a legged-robots survey, cybersecurity policy, quadruped-only, non-robot talking-head generation, etc.) without opening the primary source page, and the remaining 37 were each opened and verified against their arXiv abstract page by independent review agents. Of those 37, 22 were judged in-scope; 21 were added to the README and data/papers.json (2607.18737, a NICO self-organising-map motor-primitive paper, was judged in-scope by its reviewer but withheld by the maintenance run as too weak a fit for any of the 12 sections and flagged here instead). A human may want to spot-check the 25 title-only exclusions and reconsider 2607.18737.
